newsitem.title: FRANCE: World telecoms pact shows way for air transport.
newsitem.headline: World telecoms pact shows way for air transport.

text.p: - Liberalisation of world telecommunications trade agreed earlier in 1997 could provide an example for the air transport industry, World Trade Organisation (WTO) director trade in services division, David Hartridge told a world airports conference on Monday.

"There is a real intellectual difficulty in appplying most favoured nation (MFN) concept to the aviation sector, for instance how do you allocate landing slots on a non-discriminatory basis among the airlines of the WTO's 130 members," he told the annual meeting of Airports Council International (ACI).

"But the telecommunications negotiations also had to deal with a physically limited resource. Radio frequency is more absolutely limited than landing slots; you can't build more of it. But the allocation of radio frequency is subject to MFN," he added.

"This doesn't mean that all applications for radio have to be granted. They can't be. But it does mean that the criteria by which they have to granted are fair, objective and transparent. The same could apply to landing rights."

"But even if we accept that especially for scheduled services, landing rights are very difficult to negotiate multilaterally, there are many other aviation sources for which this is not true," he said.
For example, "The air cargo sector will come under pressure to liberalise; some of the biggest cargo handling firms are already pushing for action," Hartridge added.

He added that under the next General Agreement on Trade in Service(GATS) negotiations -- resulting from the 1994 Uruguay Round -- governments have specifically agreed to discuss air and maritime transport.
"The pressure to liberalise will be there, and efficient service providers, in whatever sector of the (air transport) industry should be thinking about how to take advantage of it," he said.
